statement: For finite weakly reversible reaction complexes with positive mass-action rate constants, F(x)=min_{y<=x} log((x-y)!) obeys F(x-y+y')-F(x)<=log(M(x)/x_under_y) for every enabled y->y', where M(x)=max_{z<=x} x_under_z; the embedded event chain has an exponential upward envelope with a rate-dependent constant.
assumptions: finite species and reaction-complex set
positive fixed rate constants
falling-factorial mass-action propensities
embedded reaction-event chain defined at nonabsorbing states
status: source-reported exact mechanism and independently reconstructed algebra; not a recurrence/nonexplosion theorem

novelty_boundary: The result controls upward changes measured by reaction events; it supplies no negative Foster drift or physical-time holding-time control, so weakly reversible positive recurrence remains open under these hypotheses.

statement: One deterministic stoichiometric class with a common global attractor can contain infinitely many closed irreducible positive recurrent stochastic classes whose stationary laws are not a uniformly tight family.
assumptions: Unit-rate mass-action stochastic model with falling-factorial propensities
Network 2C -> A+B+C -> 3A+2B -> 2C and 2C <-> 2C+D
Compare classes Gamma_n inside the same stoichiometric plane B+C=2
status: internally reconstructed explicit counterexample; source-reported in Astra summary; novelty and external priority UNKNOWN
proof_path: For each n, the class has three A/B/C phases with rates 2, n+1, 2(n+1)(n+2)(n+3), and a modulated D birth-death coordinate. Product stationary law has phase weights proportional to (1/2,1/(n+1),1/[2(n+1)(n+2)(n+3)]) times Pois(1); E[A]>=n. Each fixed-n chain is nonexplosive and positive recurrent. The deterministic network is complex-balanced at (1,1,1,1).
novelty_boundary: Refutes class-uniform tightness only; does not refute componentwise positive recurrence. Product-form stationary laws and the complex-balanced global-attractor theorem are established prior art; example novelty not established.
